title: Electrolysis of brine
caption: In concentrated sodium chloride solution, hydrogen forms at the cathode instead of sodium, because H⁺ from water is reduced more easily than Na⁺. Chlorine forms at the anode because chloride is concentrated. Sodium hydroxide is left in solution.
alt: A cell of brine with a d.c. supply: hydrogen bubbles at the negative electrode, chlorine at the positive electrode.
description: Left in solution: Na⁺ and OH⁻, sodium hydroxide.
